metadata.title: Alphabet explores first Hong Kong and Singapore dollar bond sales worth up to $3 billion

content.text:
Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG), the Google parent company, is exploring its first Hong Kong and Singapore dollar bond sales worth up to $3 billion combined.
The technology group is targeting between $1 billion and $1.5 billion from Hong Kong dollar-denominated bonds and approximately $1.5 billion from Singapore dollar notes, in US dollar-equivalent terms.
The proceeds would be used for general corporate purposes, with the potential transactions extending Alphabet's increasingly international debt issuance programme.
Wedbush views borrowing in foreign currencies and markets as a sensible approach for hyperscalers, given their expanding data centre construction programmes overseas.
The broker identifies two main drivers behind the strategy: investment in data centres across international markets and less favourable financing terms in traditional debt markets.
Alphabet's latest plans follow a €6 billion euro-denominated bond offering last week, which reportedly carried higher borrowing costs than its May issuance.
The company has also issued debt in Japanese yen and Australian dollars earlier this year, reflecting its growing use of international capital markets.
Wedbush said the latest development also highlighted the increasing scrutiny facing data centre financing.
The scale of investment required to build infrastructure supporting cloud computing and artificial intelligence has made funding arrangements an increasingly important consideration for major technology companies.
The move into Hong Kong and Singapore dollar markets would give Alphabet access to additional pools of capital while diversifying its funding sources beyond conventional debt markets.
However, the growing frequency of overseas borrowing also underlines the scale of financing required to support the technology industry's infrastructure expansion.
